items.title: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
items.summary: Scott Helme explains how eight eMudhra certificate authority private keys were compromised because they were weak single-byte elliptic-curve keys instead of random 384-bit numbers, letting anyone recover them in under a second. The keys were reported on October 17, and Chrome and Mozilla have since blocked the affected intermediates and are removing the eMudhra root from their trust stores.

items.title: Whatever Happened to Fire Escapes
items.summary: Practical Engineering looks at how external fire escapes became a fixture of American cities in the late 1800s as tall buildings multiplied and catastrophic fires were common. The piece traces why they have slowly disappeared, framing their decline as a case study in how building codes set society's consensus on what level of safety is worth the cost.

items.title: The 1.5°C goal of the Paris Agreement is no longer viable
items.summary: The UN Environment Programme's 2026 Emissions Gap Report says the chance to limit warming to 1.5°C with no or limited overshoot has been lost, and exceeding the threshold is now imminent and inevitable. UNEP states the only remaining option is to keep warming below 2°C with the aim of bringing temperatures back down to 1.5°C by the end of the century.
